question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y-1}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{y-1}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx]\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[-\operatorname{cos}⁡x]_{y-1}^{0}\,dy \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}(\operatorname{cos}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡(y-1))\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(y-1)-1)\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(y-1)-1)\,dy & =[\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-1)-y]_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)-1)-(\operatorname{sin}⁡(-1)-0) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(1)-1\end{aligned}
$$
